answer: Relay Path Accumulation.** Each agent keeps a signed relic of prior interactions, and routing only accepts peers whose accumulated path shows distinct relay neighborhoods. A voyage across many independent clusters raises trust; any address whose traffic returns to the same tight cluster is capped. To place many identities near a harbor of honest nodes, an attacker must rent diverse relays across many regions, paying per-region link costs and latency, so each successful identity carries real recurring overhead.
